# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver & Protection Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built from official New Zealand Crown and statutory releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Jonathan Palliser, FSP1004725), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: HLF (Home Loan Factory) (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Reuse Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for HLF-derived figures & commentary; official statistics credited to their respective Crown publishers.
> Date Standard: Observation Period (latest monthly: September 2026) | Period End | Source Publication Date | Last Checked (10 November 2026 / 2026-11-10).
> Active datasets: 54.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Records (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (54 Active Datasets)
- [ACC Earners' Levy rate, maximum liable earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling (Obs: 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026) | End: 2026-04-30 | Published: 2026-04-01 (1 April 2026 — 2026/27 ACC Earners' Levy schedule effective date))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/): For the 2026/27 tax year, the statutory ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) (up from $1.67 in 2025/26) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (up from $152,790, for a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22)—setting ACC's maximum 80% weekly compensation ceiling at an HLF-derived $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross). [Official Data: ACC / IRD 2026/27 Statutory Schedule: Earners' levy = $1.75 per $100 incl. GST ($1.52 excl. GST); Maximum liable earnings = $156,641 (vs $152,790 in 2025/26). | HLF Calculation: Max Levy: ($156,641 ÷ 100) × $1.75 = $2,741.22/yr | Max 80% Comp: $156,641 × 80% = $125,312.80/yr ($2,409.86/wk) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC Earners' Levy rate, maximum liable earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling," 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026). Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation (Earners' Levy) Regulations & Inland Revenue PAYE Schedule (2026/27). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims (Obs: 2025/26 ACC Financial Year | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: 2026-10-29 (29 October 2026 — ACC Annual Report 2025/26 release))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/): In the 2025/26 financial year, ACC recorded two distinct annual claim volumes: over 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims across New Zealand (up 1.6% year-on-year, mostly minor treatment-only visits) and 105,000 new weekly income compensation entitlement claims for time off work (down 1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25—an HLF-calculated ratio of 5.0 weekly compensation claims per 100 accepted injury claims). [Official Data: ACC Annual Report (2025/26): Total accepted injury claims = 2,100,000+ (+1.6% YoY, including minor treatment-only claims); New weekly compensation entitlement claims = 105,000 (-1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25). | HLF Calculation: 105,000 new weekly compensation claims ÷ 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims = 5.0 per 100 accepted claims (separate annual claim counts) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims," 2025/26 ACC Financial Year. Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report (2025/26). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Average gross borrower income on approved FHB mortgage applications (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): Based on HLF's calculation across RBNZ Table C41's five Debt-to-Income bands ($383.0m total band gross income divided by 2,655.4 implied applications), approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income in September 2026 (with official RBNZ band averages ranging from $123,000 to $197,000). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps). | HLF Calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income on approved FHB mortgage applications," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C41. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]

[Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Purchase of newly built home = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Dwelling (building) insurance annual price inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after reference quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, Stats NZ's Consumers Price Index recorded a +14.6% annual increase in the dwelling (building) insurance price index—sitting +10.9 percentage points above headline CPI inflation (3.7%). Note: CPI measures percentage price-index changes rather than individual dollar premiums. [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Dwelling insurance price index = +14.6% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.7% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Dwelling insurance CPI (+14.6%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.7%) = +10.9 percentage points | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. Note: CPI measures percentage price-index movements rather than individual policy quotes. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments. | HLF Calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up lending value = $962m across 9,639 borrowers. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported $962m of top-up lending × $1m ÷ 9,639 borrowers = $99,803 mean | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [First-home buyers approved at <=80% LVR (20% or greater deposit) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 1,325 first-home buyers ($680m) approved at &le;80% LVR (corresponding to a 20% or greater deposit)—representing an HLF-derived 49.7% share of first-home approvals and a mean loan size of $513,208. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,325 <=80% LVR FHB borrowers ($680m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers. | HLF Calculation: 1,325 ÷ 2,667 = 49.7% (Mean loan: $680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "First-home buyers approved at <=80% LVR (20% or greater deposit)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/ (checked 10 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Over the 12 months to September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded an HLF-derived rolling total of 33,485 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $19.61B in lending (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 borrowers (47.0%) approved at &gt;80% LVR (under a 20% deposit). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (12 months to September 2026): Sum of monthly FHB approvals = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR FHB approvals = 15,743 loans. | HLF Calculation: 12-month sum = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR share = 15,743 ÷ 33,485 = 47.0% | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals," September 2026. - [First-home buyer share of all >80% LVR mortgage lending (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-bank-lvr-priority/): In September 2026, first-home buyers accounted for an HLF-derived 67.2% of all &gt;80% LVR mortgage dollars ($850m of $1.26B) and 62.0% of &gt;80% LVR loans (1,342 of 2,165) reported in RBNZ Table C31. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): FHB >80% LVR = $850m (1,342 loans); All Borrower >80% LVR = $1,264m (2,165 loans). | HLF Calculation: Dollars: $850m ÷ $1,264m = 67.2% | Loans: 1,342 ÷ 2,165 = 62.0% | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [First-home buyer average mortgage size by LVR tier (>80% LVR vs <=80% LVR) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-loan-size-gap/): In September 2026, the HLF-derived mean mortgage size for first-home buyers at &gt;80% LVR (under 20% deposit) was $633,383 (1,342 loans / $850m), compared with $513,208 for first-home buyers at &le;80% LVR (1,325 loans / $680m)—an HLF-calculated difference of $120,175 (derived from RBNZ Table C31 dollar series rounded to $1m). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): >80% LVR FHB = $850m across 1,342 borrowers; <=80% LVR FHB = $680m across 1,325 borrowers (dollar series rounded to $1m). | HLF Calculation: ($850m × $1m ÷ 1,342 = $633,383) minus ($680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) = $120,175 (subject to RBNZ $1m rounding) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: Inland Revenue Regional KiwiSaver Withdrawals (Year ended 30 June 2026): 50,330 members withdrew $2,265,097,300 across 16 NZ regions. | HLF Calculation: $2,265,097,300 ÷ 50,330 members = $45,005/member (Regional range: $39,916–$50,364) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory.
